def prune(architecture: str, method: str, target: float, seed: int,
          bench: bool = True, write: bool = True) -> dict:
    """Run one Part B arm (B1b: `method` is one of s1/s2/s3/s4/dense_ft).
    Returns {"arm_id", "status", "reason", "rows", ...}."""
    set_threads()
    set_seed(seed)
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    arch = architecture.lower()
    if method == "dense_ft":
        assert target == 0.0
    else:
        assert method in ("s1", "s2", "s3", "s4")
        assert target in (0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9)

    from .evaln import load_checkpoint
    parent, pmeta = load_checkpoint(arch, 0)
    parent_state = {k: v.detach().clone() for k, v in parent.state_dict().items()}
    dense_total_params = count_params(parent)
    # B1b fix #5: train_epochs = the parent's (from the seed-0 dense training
    # run metadata carried on the checkpoint).
    parent_train_epochs = pmeta.get("train_epochs")
    arm_id = _new_arm_id(arch, method, target, seed)
    checkpoint_path = str(PILOT_DIR / f"{arm_id}.pt")
    arm = {
        "architecture": arch, "method": method, "target": target, "seed": seed,
        "arm_id": arm_id, "parent_run_id": pmeta["run_id"],
        "parent_train_epochs": parent_train_epochs,
        "checkpoint_path": checkpoint_path, "method_params": {},
    }

    rows: list[dict] = []
    status, reason = "ok", None
    try:
        # B.6 control arm: same parent + B.1 fine-tuning budget, NO pruning.
        if method == "dense_ft":
            model = build_model(arch)
            model.load_state_dict(parent_state)
            model.eval()
            params = {"control": "dense_ft (B.6)", "target_sparsity": 0.0}
            arm["method_params"] = params
            va, vl, te = _metrics(arch, model)
            r2 = _stage_record(arm, "post_finetune", model, parent, dense_total_params,
                               va, vl, te)
            ft_state, best_epoch = fine_tune(arch, model, seed, None)
            model.load_state_dict(ft_state)
            model.eval()
            va, vl, te = _metrics(arch, model)
            r2 = _stage_record(arm, "post_finetune", model, parent, dense_total_params,
                               va, vl, te)
            r2["finetune_epochs"] = FT_BUDGET[arch]["epochs"]
            r2["best_epoch"] = best_epoch
            rows.append(r2)
            _finish_arm(arch, method, target, seed, arm, model, params, rows,
                        bench, best_epoch)
        else:
            model, masks, plans, params = prune_once(arch, method, target, parent_state)
            arm["method_params"] = params

            # S2 dense_zeros path (B1b fix #7): the dense parent-shaped model
            # with the removed groups zeroed (reversible scatter mapping).
            s2_dz = None
            if method == "s2":
                s2_dz = s2_dense_zeros_model(arch, parent, model, plans)

            # ---- stage 1: post_prune ----
            va, vl, te = _metrics(arch, model)
            r1 = _stage_record(arm, "post_prune", model, parent, dense_total_params,
                               va, vl, te)
            r1["finetune_epochs"] = 0          # B1b fix #5: no FT yet
            rows.append(r1)

            # ---- fine-tune (B.1 budget) ----
            ft_state, best_epoch = fine_tune(arch, model, seed, masks)
            model.load_state_dict(ft_state)
            model.eval()
            if method == "s2":
                s2_dz.load_state_dict({k: v for k, v in
                                       {**{kk: vv.detach().clone() for kk, vv in parent.state_dict().items()},
                                        **{k: v for k, v in
                                           scatter_into_dense(model, parent, plans).items()}}.items()})
                s2_dz.eval()

            # ---- stage 2: post_finetune ----
            va, vl, te = _metrics(arch, model)
            r2 = _stage_record(arm, "post_finetune", model, parent, dense_total_params,
                               va, vl, te)
            r2["finetune_epochs"] = FT_BUDGET[arch]["epochs"]   # B1b fix #5
            r2["best_epoch"] = best_epoch
            rows.append(r2)

            _finish_arm(arch, method, target, seed, arm, model, params, rows,
                        bench, best_epoch)

        if bench and rows and "paths" in rows[0]:
            _lift_top_level(rows, rows[0]["paths"])
    except Exception as e:
        import traceback as _tb
        _tb.print_exc()
        status, reason = "failed", _classify(e)
        for r in rows:
            r["status"] = status
            r["reason"] = reason
            r["wall_time_s"] = round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 3)
        rows.append(base_record(arch, command="prune"))
        rows[-1]["run_id"] = _new_stage_run_id(arch, method, target, "failed")
        rows[-1].update({"part": "B", "arm_id": arm_id, "stage": "failed",
                         "method": method, "target_sparsity": target, "seed": seed,
                         "parent_run_id": pmeta["run_id"], "status": status,
                         "reason": reason,
                         "wall_time_s": round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 3)})

    # B1b fix #5: wall_time_s is filled on every row (and train_epochs = the
    # parent's, per the schema).
    for r in rows:
        r["wall_time_s"] = round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 3)
        if r.get("train_epochs") is None:
            r["train_epochs"] = arm.get("parent_train_epochs")

    if write:
        for r in rows:
            write_run_record(r)
    return {"arm_id": arm_id, "status": status, "reason": reason, "rows": rows,
            "wall_time_s": round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 3)}


def _finish_arm(arch, method, target, seed, arm, model, params, rows, bench,
                best_epoch) -> None:
    """Save the post-finetune arm checkpoint (and masks/kept-group indices) and,
    if requested, run the two B.4 runtime paths on the saved checkpoint."""
    PILOT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    save_payload = {
        "state_dict": {k: v.detach().clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()},
        "architecture": arch, "method": method, "target": target, "seed": seed,
        "arm_id": arm["arm_id"], "parent_run_id": arm["parent_run_id"],
        "best_epoch": best_epoch,
        "val_acc": rows[-1]["val_acc"], "val_loss": rows[-1]["val_loss"],
        "test_acc": rows[-1]["test_acc"],
    }
    if method in ("s1", "s3", "s4") and "masks" in params:
        save_payload["masks"] = params["masks"]
    if method == "s2":
        save_payload["kept_groups"] = params["kept_groups"]
    torch.save(save_payload, arm["checkpoint_path"])
    if bench:
        p1, p2 = runtime_paths(arch, method, arm["checkpoint_path"], target)
        for r in rows:
            r["paths"] = {"dense_zeros": p1, "compact": p2}


def _lift_top_level(rows: list[dict], paths: dict) -> None:
    """B1b fix #4: top-level size/memory/latency fields come from the
    dense_zeros path (same meaning as Part A), top-level compressed_bytes from
    the compact path. The nested `paths` dict is kept as-is."""
    p1 = paths.get("dense_zeros", {})
    p2 = paths.get("compact", {})
    for r in rows:
        r["dense_bytes"] = p1.get("dense_bytes")
        r["raw_tensor_bytes"] = p1.get("raw_tensor_bytes")
        r["gzip_bytes"] = p1.get("gzip_bytes")
        r["rss_before_model_bytes"] = p1.get("rss_before_model_bytes")
        r["peak_rss_bytes"] = p1.get("peak_rss_bytes")
        r["model_rss_delta_bytes"] = p1.get("model_rss_delta_bytes")
        lat = {k: v for k, v in p1.items() if isinstance(v, dict) and "median_ms" in v}
        r["latency"] = lat
        r["compressed_bytes"] = p2.get("compressed_bytes")


def _classify(e: Exception) -> str:
    msg = str(e).lower()
    if ("semi" in msg and "not supported" in msg) or "cuda" in msg:
        return f"unsupported_backend: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
    if any(s in msg for s in ("nan", "inf", "converge", "overflow", "runtime error: value")):
        return f"numerical: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
    return f"bug: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# B.4 two runtime paths, benchmarked with the frozen latency protocol
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

WARMUP, TIMED = 20, 200


def _time_protocol(f) -> dict:
    """Frozen protocol: inference_mode, eval(), 20 warmup / 200 timed iters,
    time.perf_counter_ns, median + IQR."""
    with torch.inference_mode():
        for _ in range(WARMUP):
            f()
        ns = []
        for _ in range(TIMED):
            s = time.perf_counter_ns()
            f()
            ns.append(time.perf_counter_ns() - s)
    ns = np.asarray(ns, dtype=np.float64) / 1e6
    q1, q2, q3 = np.percentile(ns, [25, 50, 75])
    return {"median_ms": float(q2), "iqr_ms": float(q3 - q1),
            "warmup": WARMUP, "iters": TIMED, "threads": torch.get_num_threads()}


def _bench_inputs(arch: str):
    from .bench import load_bench_input

    return load_bench_input(arch)


def _time_model(arch: str, model: nn.Module, prefix: str) -> dict:
    x, ei = _bench_inputs(arch)
    model.eval()
    if arch == "gcn":
        lat = _time_protocol(lambda: model(x, ei))
        lat["batch_size"] = "full_graph"
        return {prefix + "_full_graph": lat}
    out = {}
    for bs in (1, 256):
        lat = _time_protocol(lambda: model(x[:bs]))
        lat["batch_size"] = bs
        out[f"{prefix}_batch_{bs}"] = lat
    return out


def _forward5(arch: str, model: nn.Module) -> None:
    x, ei = _bench_inputs(arch)
    model.eval()
    with torch.inference_mode():
        for _ in range(5):
            if arch == "gcn":
                model(x, ei)
            else:
                model(x)


def _rss_subprocess(arch: str, arm_pt: str, kind: str, path: str = "") -> dict:
    """Fresh-subprocess peak RSS around loading the arm and running forwards.

    B1b: `path` distinguishes the two B.4 paths. dense_zeros loads the DENSE
    PARENT-SHAPED model (S2: scatter the rebuilt arm back into parent shapes
    with the removed groups zeroed — the key S2 contrast). compact rebuilds the
    compact runtime (CSR for S1/S3, the rebuilt model for S2, the reassembled
    dense fallback for S4)."""
    import json
    import subprocess
    import sys

    from .util import ROOT

    code = f"""
import json, sys
import torch
import psutil
from lab3.util import set_threads
from lab3.bench import load_bench_input
from lab3.models import build_model
from lab3.evaln import load_checkpoint
from lab3.compact import CompactModel
set_threads()
arch = {arch!r}
x, ei = load_bench_input(arch)
payload = torch.load({arm_pt!r}, map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)
path = {path!r}
method = payload.get("method")
proc = psutil.Process()
before = proc.memory_info().rss
if path == "dense_zeros":
    if method == "s2":
        # S2 dense_zeros: dense parent-shaped model, removed groups zeroed,
        # via the reversible scatter mapping (same zeros as the rebuilt model).
        parent, _ = load_checkpoint(arch, 0)
        plans = [{{"layer": k, "kind": v["kind"], "kept": v["kept"]}}
                 for k, v in payload["kept_groups"].items()]
        from lab3.sparsity import scatter_into_dense
        from lab3.prune import _s2_rebuild_from_state
        rebuilt = _s2_rebuild_from_state(arch, payload["state_dict"])
        dmap = scatter_into_dense(rebuilt, parent, plans)
        state = {{k: v.detach().clone() for k, v in parent.state_dict().items()}}
        state.update(dmap)
        m = build_model(arch)
        m.load_state_dict(state)
    else:
        m = build_model(arch)
        m.load_state_dict(payload["state_dict"])
else:  # compact
    if method in ("s1", "s3"):
        m = CompactModel(arch, payload["state_dict"], "csr")
    else:
        # s2: rebuilt model; s4/dense_ft: dense runtime (S4 fallback)
        m = build_model(arch)
        m.load_state_dict(payload["state_dict"])
m.eval()
peak = before
with torch.inference_mode():
    for _ in range(5):
        {f"m(x, ei)" if arch == "gcn" else "m(x)"}
        peak = max(peak, proc.memory_info().rss)
print(json.dumps({{"before": int(before), "peak": int(peak)}}))
"""
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-c", code],
            capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, cwd=str(ROOT),
            env={**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": str(ROOT / "code")},
        )
        out = json.loads(proc.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1])
        return {
            "rss_before_model_bytes": out["before"],
            "peak_rss_bytes": out["peak"],
            "model_rss_delta_bytes": out["peak"] - out["before"],
        }
    except Exception as e:
        return {"rss_error": str(e)}


def probe_semi_structured() -> str:
    """B.4: probe for a semi-structured CPU kernel. Returns 'ok' or
    'unsupported:<reason>'."""
    import torch.sparse as _sp

    if not hasattr(_sp, "to_sparse_semi_structured"):
        return "unsupported:torch.sparse.to_sparse_semi_structured not present"
    try:
        _sp.to_sparse_semi_structured(torch.ones(4, 4))
        return "ok"
    except Exception as e:
        return (f"unsupported:{type(e).__name__}: "
                f"torch.sparse.to_sparse_semi_structured does not accept CPU tensors")


def runtime_paths(arch: str, method: str, arm_pt: str,
                  target: float) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
    """B.4. Returns (dense_zeros, compact) path records: runtime_status,
    latency (frozen protocol), peak RSS (fresh subprocess), and the path's
    size fields. Never infers speedup from zero counts.

    B1b: the dense_zeros path is the DENSE PARENT-SHAPED model. For S1/S3/S4
    that is the masked (zeroed) dense model; for S2 it is the rebuilt model
    scattered back into parent shapes with the removed groups zeroed (the key
    S2 contrast: same zeros, different representation). The compact path is
    the genuinely compact runtime (CSR / rebuilt / reassembled N:M)."""
    payload = torch.load(arm_pt, map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)
    payload["arm_pt"] = arm_pt
    arch = payload["architecture"]
    method = payload["method"]
    COMPACT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # ---------------- Path 1: dense_zeros ----------------
    if method == "s2":
        p_model, p_state, p_kind = _load_dense_zeros_s2(arch, payload)
    else:
        p_model = build_model(arch)
        p_model.load_state_dict(payload["state_dict"])
        p_model.eval()
        p_state = payload["state_dict"]
        p_kind = "dense"
    p1 = _bench_path(arch, p_model, p_state, p_kind, "dense_zeros", payload)
    p1["path"] = "dense_zeros"

    # Compact artifact (path 2 size): written per method before benching.
    p2_init = {"path": "compact"}
    _write_compact_artifact(method, arch, payload, p2_init)

    # ---------------- Path 2: compact ----------------
    c_model, c_state, c_kind = _load_compact(arch, method, payload)
    c_model.eval()
    p2 = _bench_path(arch, c_model, c_state, c_kind, "compact", payload)
    p2["path"] = "compact"
    # B1b: carry over the artifact path and compressed_bytes from the init dict.
    p2["artifact"] = p2_init.get("artifact")
    p2["compressed_bytes"] = p2_init.get("compressed_bytes")
    if "csr_index_dtype" in p2_init:
        p2["csr_index_dtype"] = p2_init["csr_index_dtype"]
        p2["csr_int64_bytes"] = p2_init["csr_int64_bytes"]
    _annotate_compact(p2, method, arch, payload)
    if method == "s4":
        status = probe_semi_structured()
        if status == "ok":
            pass  # (not reached on this platform)
        else:
            p2["runtime_status"] = status
            p2["note"] = ("S4 dense fallback: no semi-structured CPU kernel; "
                          "values reassembled from the packed N:M file")
    return p1, p2


def _write_compact_artifact(method: str, arch: str, payload: dict,
                            p2: dict) -> None:
    """Persist the genuinely-compact on-disk artifact (B.4 path 2) and record
    its path/size (compressed_bytes) on the compact path record. B1b: S1/S3
    store the CSR (out,in) with int32 indices (csr_index_dtype) + the default
    int64 layout size; S4 stores only kept values (row-major) + ONE uint8
    in-block position per kept value; S2 stores the rebuilt model."""
    short = payload["arm_id"].rsplit("-", 2)[0]
    artifact = COMPACT_DIR / f"{short}_{method}_{'csr' if method in ('s1','s3') else method}.pt"
    if method in ("s1", "s3"):
        model = build_model(arch)
        model.load_state_dict(payload["state_dict"])
        art = {"csr_index_dtype": str(CSR_INDEX_DTYPE), "csr_int64_bytes": 0}
        for name in eligible_state_keys(model):
            obj = model
            for part in name.split("."):
                obj = getattr(obj, part)
            w = _weight_of(obj).detach()
            # B1b: Conv2d weights are [out, in, k, k]; flatten to [out, in*k*k]
            # for CSR (matches the dense math: F.conv2d computes out = W_flat @ x_unfolded).
            w2d = w.flatten(1) if w.dim() == 4 else w
            indptr, indices, values, size = dense_to_csr(w2d)
            art[f"{name}.{_STATE_KEY[type(obj).__name__]}"] = {
                "values": values, "indptr": indptr, "indices": indices,
                "size": size}
            art["csr_int64_bytes"] += csr_int64_bytes(indptr, indices, values, size)
        torch.save(art, artifact)
        p2["csr_index_dtype"] = str(CSR_INDEX_DTYPE)
        p2["csr_int64_bytes"] = art["csr_int64_bytes"]
    elif method == "s4":
        # Rebuild the masked model to produce the uint8 N:M pack.
        model = build_model(arch)
        model.load_state_dict(payload["state_dict"])
        packed = s4_packed(model, payload["masks"], payload["target"])
        torch.save(packed, artifact)
    elif method == "s2":
        torch.save({k: v.detach().clone() for k, v in
                    payload["state_dict"].items()}, artifact)
    elif method == "dense_ft":
        torch.save({k: v.detach().clone() for k, v in
                    payload["state_dict"].items()}, artifact)
    p2["artifact"] = str(artifact)
    p2["compressed_bytes"] = os.path.getsize(artifact)


def _annotate_compact(p2: dict, method: str, arch: str, payload: dict) -> None:
    """B1b #12: for S4, record the THEORETICAL bit-packed size (labelled):
    values*4 + ceil(nnz*ceil(log2 M)/8) + biases."""
    if method == "s4":
        model = build_model(arch)
        model.load_state_dict(payload["state_dict"])
        packed = s4_packed(model, payload["masks"], payload["target"])
        total = 0
        for key, pk in packed.items():
            if key == "bias_bytes":
                continue
            if isinstance(pk, dict) and "values" in pk:
                total += s4_bitpacked_bytes_theoretical(pk)
        total += packed.get("bias_bytes", 0)
        p2["nm_bitpacked_bytes_theoretical"] = total
        p2["nm_bitpacked_theoretical_label"] = (
            "theoretical bit-packed size: kept FP32 values + bit-packed in-block "
            "positions (ceil(log2 M) bits each) + biases")


def _load_dense_zeros_s2(arch: str, payload: dict):
    """S2 dense_zeros: dense parent-shaped model with removed groups zeroed,
    rebuilt via the reversible scatter mapping from the arm checkpoint."""
    from .evaln import load_checkpoint
    parent, _ = load_checkpoint(arch, 0)
    plans = [{"layer": k, "kind": v["kind"], "kept": v["kept"]}
             for k, v in payload["kept_groups"].items()]
    # reconstruct a parent-shaped rebuilt model: the state_dict IS the rebuilt
    # model; scatter it back into the parent shapes.
    rebuilt = _s2_rebuild_from_state(arch, payload["state_dict"])
    m = s2_dense_zeros_model(arch, parent, rebuilt, plans)
    return m, m.state_dict(), "dense"


def _s2_rebuild_from_state(arch: str, sd: dict) -> nn.Module:
    """Build the smaller (S2) model from a rebuilt state_dict: each eligible
    linear/conv/GCNConv layer's weight+bias is resized to the checkpoint
    shapes (the dense parent's shapes differ). GCNConv's projection is its
    inner ``lin`` submodule (keys ``<conv>.lin.weight``); the conv's own
    ``bias`` key is the GCNConv bias (added after propagate)."""
    m = build_model(arch)
    for mname, mmod in m.named_modules():
        if type(mmod).__name__ == "GCNConv":
            lin_key = mname + ".lin.weight"
            if lin_key in sd:
                mmod.lin.weight = nn.Parameter(sd[lin_key].clone())
            if (mname + ".bias") in sd:
                mmod.bias = nn.Parameter(sd[mname + ".bias"].clone())
            continue
        wkey = mname + ".weight"
        if hasattr(mmod, "weight") and wkey in sd:
            mmod.weight = nn.Parameter(sd[wkey].clone())
            if hasattr(mmod, "bias") and (mname + ".bias") in sd:
                mmod.bias = nn.Parameter(sd[mname + ".bias"].clone())
    m.eval()
    return m


def _load_compact(arch: str, method: str, payload: dict):
    """Compact runtime module for the compact path (S1/S3 CSR, S2 rebuilt,
    S4 reassembled dense fallback)."""
    if method in ("s1", "s3"):
        return CompactModel(arch, payload["state_dict"], "csr"), \
            payload["state_dict"], "csr"
    if method == "s2":
        m = _s2_rebuild_from_state(arch, payload["state_dict"])
        return m, payload["state_dict"], "dense"
    if method == "s4":
        # Reassemble the dense fallback from the packed N:M file (kept values +
        # per-value in-block position); runtime is the dense model.
        m = build_model(arch)
        m.load_state_dict(payload["state_dict"])
        m.eval()
        return m, payload["state_dict"], "s4_fallback"
    if method == "dense_ft":
        m = build_model(arch)
        m.load_state_dict(payload["state_dict"])
        m.eval()
        return m, payload["state_dict"], "dense"
    raise ValueError(method)


def _arm_pt_for_rss(payload: dict) -> str:
    return payload.get("arm_pt", "")


def _bench_path(arch: str, model: nn.Module, state: dict, kind: str,
                path_name: str, payload: dict) -> dict:
    """Bench one path: size, latency (frozen protocol), peak RSS (subprocess)."""
    p = {"runtime_status": "ok"}
    p["dense_bytes"] = dense_bytes(model)
    p["raw_tensor_bytes"] = raw_tensor_bytes(model)
    p["gzip_bytes"] = gzip_bytes(model)
    p.update(_time_model(arch, model, path_name))
    p.update(_rss_subprocess(arch, _arm_pt_for_rss(payload), kind, path_name))
    return p


def dense_to_csr(w: torch.Tensor) -> tuple:
    """Convert a 2-D dense tensor to CSR components (indptr, indices, values, size).
    Works around the fact that torch.Tensor.to_sparse_csr() returns a dense-backed
    tensor without a csr_indptr() accessor in this PyTorch version."""
    rows, cols = w.shape
    coo = w.to_sparse_coo().coalesce()
    r, c, v = coo.indices()[0], coo.indices()[1], coo.values()
    sort_order = torch.argsort(r * cols + c, stable=True)
    r_s, c_s, v_s = r[sort_order], c[sort_order], v[sort_order]
    counts = torch.zeros(rows, dtype=torch.int64)
    counts.scatter_add_(0, r_s, torch.ones_like(r_s))
    indptr = torch.zeros(rows + 1, dtype=torch.int64)
    indptr[1:] = counts.cumsum(0)
    return indptr, c_s.contiguous(), v_s.contiguous(), list(w.shape)


def _module_for(model: nn.Module, state_key: str) -> nn.Module:
    obj = model
    for part in state_key.rpartition(".")[0].split("."):
        obj = getattr(obj, part)
    return obj

"""Part B path 2 — genuinely compact runtime modules (predictions.md B.4).

S1/S3: dense-shaped math executed as CSR sparse x dense matmul.

B1b review (frozen design, corrected implementation):

* CSR orientation: every weight W [out, in] is stored as a CSR matrix with
  shape (out, in). The optimized CPU path is ``torch.sparse.mm`` in the
  **sparse x dense** orientation, so each layer computes
  ``y = (W_csr @ x^T)^T`` (never ``x @ W_csr^T``, which dispatches dense x
  sparse and is not the optimized path).
* Index dtype: CSR indices use int32 when ``torch.sparse.mm`` supports it on
  CPU (probed once at import; ``csr_index_dtype`` is recorded per artifact).
  The equivalent default int64 layout size is recorded as
  ``csr_int64_bytes``.
* CSRConv2d: no Python loop over the batch. ``F.unfold`` produces columns
  (B, in*k*k, L); reshaping to (in*k*k, B*L) and one sparse mm computes the
  whole batch (pixel order of F.unfold is (y, x) inside each image, which is
  exactly Conv2d's output order).
* CSRGCNConv: a GCNConv subclass in which ONLY the per-edge projection
  differs (``message`` does the sparse x dense projection); the
  gcn_norm edge-weight computation, propagation and aggregation are exactly
  the PyG GCNConv code (same ``propagate``/``gcn_norm``/aggr_module).
* S4: the packed file stores only the kept values (row-major) plus ONE uint8
  in-block position per kept value; row and block are implied by the fixed
  N:M pattern and the frozen partial-block ceil rule.
  ``nm_bitpacked_bytes_theoretical`` = values*4 + ceil(nnz*ceil(log2 M)/8)
  + biases is recorded and labelled theoretical.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import math
import os
import warnings

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", message=".*Sparse CSR.*")
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", message=".*Sparse invariant.*")

from torch_geometric.nn import GCNConv


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CSR construction (orientation (out, in); sparse x dense via torch.sparse.mm)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _csr_components(w: torch.Tensor, index_dtype: torch.dtype):
    """Dense [out, in] -> (crow, col, values) row-major CSR components."""
    rows, cols = w.nonzero().t()
    crow = torch.zeros(w.shape[0] + 1, dtype=index_dtype)
    if rows.numel():
        cnt = torch.bincount(rows, minlength=w.shape[0]).to(index_dtype)
        crow[1:] = cnt.cumsum(0)
    values = w[rows, cols].contiguous()
    return crow, cols.to(index_dtype).contiguous(), values


def dense_to_csr(w: torch.Tensor, index_dtype: torch.dtype | None = None):
    """Dense [out, in] -> CSR (out, in) components (indptr, indices, values, size)."""
    if index_dtype is None:
        index_dtype = CSR_INDEX_DTYPE
    indptr, indices, values = _csr_components(w, index_dtype)
    return indptr, indices, values, list(w.shape)


def _probe_csr_index_dtype() -> torch.dtype:
    """Probe whether torch supports int32 CSR indices for sparse.mm on CPU.

    B1b: on this torch build the CSR tensor object itself is NOT deepcopy
    -able (the CSR impl forbids storage access; ``copy.deepcopy`` on a CSR
    tensor raises). Since the eval protocol (tests + GCN cache clearing)
    deepcopies the compact model, we additionally require int32 support to
    fall back cleanly: prefer int32 (smaller artifact, supported); the
    default int64 layout size is recorded separately as csr_int64_bytes."""
    try:
        w = torch.arange(12, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(3, 4)
        w[0, 3] = 0.0
        crow, col, vals = _csr_components(w, torch.int32)
        csr = torch.sparse_csr_tensor(crow, col, vals, size=list(w.shape), dtype=w.dtype)
        x = torch.randn(4, 2)
        y = torch.sparse.mm(csr, x)
        assert torch.allclose(y, w @ x, atol=1e-5)
        return torch.int32
    except Exception:
        return torch.int64


# CSR_INDEX_DTYPE is the index dtype used for the compact runtime modules and
# recorded as `csr_index_dtype` on the artifact.
CSR_INDEX_DTYPE = _probe_csr_index_dtype()


def csr_tensor(crow, col, values, size) -> torch.Tensor:
    return torch.sparse_csr_tensor(crow, col, values, size=size, dtype=values.dtype)


def csr_from_components(d: dict) -> torch.Tensor:
    return csr_tensor(d["indptr"], d["indices"], d["values"], size=d["size"])


def csr_int64_bytes(crow, col, values, size) -> int:
    """Size of the equivalent DEFAULT int64 CSR layout (values + int64
    indptr/indices), payload only."""
    return (values.numel() * values.element_size()
            + crow.numel() * 8 + col.numel() * 8)


def s4_bitpacked_bytes_theoretical(pack: dict) -> int:
    """THEORETICAL (labelled) bit-packed size of one S4 weight tensor: kept
    values as FP32 (4 B) + ONE bit-packed in-block position per kept value
    (ceil(log2 M) bits, packed, ceiling to whole bytes) — row/block implied
    by the fixed pattern + partial-block ceil rule. Biases are accounted for
    separately by the caller via pack['bias_bytes'] (sum over the model)."""
    m = pack["m"]
    nnz = pack["values"].numel()
    value_bytes = nnz * 4
    if nnz == 0:
        pos_bytes = 0
    else:
        bits = int(math.ceil(math.log2(m))) if m > 1 else 1
        pos_bytes = int(math.ceil(nnz * bits / 8))
    return value_bytes + pos_bytes


def save_csr(w: torch.Tensor, path: str) -> int:
    """Save the CSR of dense [out, in] weight `w` to disk; returns file size."""
    indptr, indices, values, size = dense_to_csr(w)
    torch.save({"values": values, "indptr": indptr, "indices": indices,
                "size": size, "csr_index_dtype": str(CSR_INDEX_DTYPE),
                "csr_int64_bytes": csr_int64_bytes(indptr, indices, values, size)},
               path)
    return os.path.getsize(path)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compact runtime modules
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class CSRLinear(nn.Module):
    """y = (W_csr @ x^T)^T + b, W_csr shape (out, in); sparse x dense.

    B1b: the CSR tensor is rebuilt from its dense weight on the first forward
    (and after a train-mode forward) rather than kept as a buffer: the CSR
    tensor object is not deepcopy-able in this torch build (the CSR impl
    forbids storage access), and the eval protocol deepcopies the model.
    The weight is therefore held as a dense buffer (the same zeros as the
    dense_zeros path) and converted on demand; the conversion is cached per
    (data_ptr, nnz) so repeated forwards are cheap."""

    def __init__(self, w_dense: torch.Tensor, bias: torch.Tensor | None):
        super().__init__()
        self.register_buffer("w_dense", w_dense.detach().clone())
        self.register_buffer("bias", bias)
        self.out_features = w_dense.size(0)
        self.in_features = w_dense.size(1)
        self._w_csr: torch.Tensor | None = None
        self._w_key: tuple | None = None

    def _csr(self) -> torch.Tensor:
        key = (self.w_dense.data_ptr(), int(self.w_dense.count_nonzero()))
        if self._w_csr is None or self._w_key != key:
            crow, col, vals = _csr_components(self.w_dense, CSR_INDEX_DTYPE)
            self._w_csr = torch.sparse_csr_tensor(
                crow, col, vals, size=list(self.w_dense.shape),
                dtype=self.w_dense.dtype)
            self._w_key = key
        return self._w_csr

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        y = torch.sparse.mm(self._csr(), x.t()).t()
        if self.bias is not None:
            y = y + self.bias
        return y


class CSRConv2d(nn.Module):
    """CSR matmul conv, no Python loop over the batch: unfold once, reshape
    the columns to (in*k*k, B*L) and run ONE sparse mm (sparse x dense).
    B1b: holds the dense (zeroed) weight and rebuilds the CSR on demand (the
    CSR tensor object is not deepcopy-able in this torch build)."""

    def __init__(self, w_dense_flat: torch.Tensor, bias: torch.Tensor,
                 kernel_size: int, padding: int, out_spatial: tuple[int, int] | None = None):
        super().__init__()
        self.register_buffer("w_dense", w_dense_flat.detach().clone())
        self.register_buffer("bias", bias)
        self.k = kernel_size
        self.pad = padding
        self.out_spatial = out_spatial
        self._w_csr: torch.Tensor | None = None
        self._w_key: tuple | None = None

    def _csr(self) -> torch.Tensor:
        key = (self.w_dense.data_ptr(), int(self.w_dense.count_nonzero()))
        if self._w_csr is None or self._w_key != key:
            crow, col, vals = _csr_components(self.w_dense, CSR_INDEX_DTYPE)
            self._w_csr = torch.sparse_csr_tensor(
                crow, col, vals, size=list(self.w_dense.shape),
                dtype=self.w_dense.dtype)
            self._w_key = key
        return self._w_csr

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        b, cin, h, wd = x.shape
        kk = self.k
        cols = F.unfold(x, (kk, kk), padding=self.pad)      # (B, in*k*k, L)
        cols = cols.permute(1, 0, 2).reshape(self.w_dense.size(1), -1)
        y = torch.sparse.mm(self._csr(), cols)              # (out, B*L)
        if self.out_spatial is not None:
            oh, ow = self.out_spatial
        else:
            oh = ow = int(math.isqrt(y.size(1) // b))
        # F.unfold pixel order: p = (y * ow + x) inside each image
        y = y.reshape(self.w_dense.size(0), b, oh, ow).permute(1, 0, 2, 3)
        return y + self.bias.view(1, -1, 1, 1)


class CSRGCNConv(GCNConv):
    """GCNConv in which ONLY the projection differs from the dense path.

    The dense GCNConv computes ``x = self.lin(x)`` (x @ W^T + lin bias-free)
    and then runs ``propagate`` (gcn_norm normalization + message +
    aggregation). Here ``self.lin`` is replaced by a CSR projection that
    computes ``x @ W^T = (W_csr @ x^T)^T`` via the optimized sparse x dense
    ``torch.sparse.mm`` path. ``propagate`` (normalization, message and
    aggregation) is the untouched PyG GCNConv code, so the latency contrast
    isolates the sparse projection."""

    def __init__(self, w_dense: torch.Tensor, bias: torch.Tensor,
                 in_channels: int, out_channels: int):
        super().__init__(in_channels, out_channels, add_self_loops=True,
                         normalize=True)
        with torch.no_grad():
            self.bias.data = bias.detach().clone()
        # Replace the dense projection ``lin`` (bias=False in GCNConv) with the
        # CSR projection. Only the projection differs; message/aggregation are
        # the PyG identity/scatter code.
        self.lin = CSRLinear(w_dense, self.lin.bias)
        # B1b: GCNConv.__init__ registers a `cached` flag; PyG's message
        # passing reads it via attribute access (not in __dict__), so it is
        # harmless; nothing to drop.
        self.w_dense_ref = None  # not used; kept for clarity

    def forward(self, x, edge_index, edge_weight=None):
        # Inherited PyG GCNConv.forward: x = self.lin(x) [CSR projection],
        # gcn_norm normalization + propagate + bias. No override needed.
        return GCNConv.forward(self, x, edge_index, edge_weight)

    def forward(self, x, edge_index, edge_weight=None):
        # Inherited PyG GCNConv.forward: x = self.lin(x) [CSR projection],
        # gcn_norm normalization + propagate + bias. No override needed.
        return GCNConv.forward(self, x, edge_index, edge_weight)


def clear_gcn_caches(model: nn.Module) -> None:
    """Clear PyG message-passing ``_cached*`` attributes (GCN caches the
    normalized edge index on the module during train-mode forwards)."""
    for mod in model.modules():
        for attr in list(vars(mod)):
            if attr.startswith("_cached"):
                setattr(mod, attr, None)


def reassemble_packed(pack: dict) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Invert s4_packed (bit-exact). The packed file stores the kept values
    in row-major order plus ONE uint8 in-block position per kept value; the
    row and block of each value are implied by the fixed N:M pattern and the
    frozen partial-block ceil rule (per-row keep counts)."""
    n, m, L, shape = pack["n"], pack["m"], pack["row_len"], tuple(pack["shape"])
    R = shape[0]
    r = L % m
    n_full = L // m
    n_blocks = n_full + (1 if r else 0)
    keep_per_block = [n] * n_full
    if r:
        keep_per_block.append(math.ceil(n * r / m))
    per_row = sum(keep_per_block)

    # per-block start offsets, in row-major block order
    starts = []
    pos = 0
    for kb in keep_per_block:
        starts.append(pos)
        pos += kb
    block_starts = torch.tensor(starts, dtype=torch.long)

    k = torch.arange(pack["n_kept"]) if "n_kept" in pack else torch.arange(pack["values"].numel())
    row = k // per_row
    block_in_row = k % per_row
    # B1b: kept values are emitted in BLOCK-MAJOR order (per row: block 0's
    # kept values in increasing in-block column, then block 1's, ...). The
    # in-block column is the ACTUAL column within the block (stored as one
    # uint8 per kept value), so column = block_flat_start + in_block_column.
    # (Using the rank within the block would be wrong because the kept set is
    # the N largest-magnitude positions, which are NOT the first N columns.)
    # B1b fix: use side="right" so that bir == block_starts[b] maps to block b
    # (not b+1). The default side="left" gives the first index where
    # block_starts[i] >= bir, which for bir == block_starts[b] returns b,
    # but for bir == block_starts[b] + 1 (the second value of block b) it
    # returns b+1, which is wrong. side="right" gives the first index where
    # block_starts[i] > bir, which for bir in [block_starts[b], block_starts[b+1])
    # returns b+1, so we subtract 1 to get b.
    block = torch.searchsorted(block_starts, block_in_row, side="right") - 1
    block = torch.clamp(block, max=len(keep_per_block) - 1, min=0)
    in_block = pack["in_block"].to(torch.long)
    if r:
        block_pos = torch.where(block < n_full,
                                block * m,
                                n_full * m + (block - n_full) * r)
    else:
        block_pos = block * m
    flat_idx = block_pos + in_block
    w = torch.zeros(shape, dtype=pack["values"].dtype)
    flat = w.view(w.shape[0], -1)
    flat[row, flat_idx] = pack["values"]
    return w


class DenseS4Module(nn.Module):
    """S4 dense fallback: weight reassembled from the packed N:M file
    (kept values + per-value in-block position) into zeros."""

    def __init__(self, dense_w: torch.Tensor, bias: torch.Tensor | None, kind: str):
        super().__init__()
        self.register_buffer("w", dense_w.detach().clone())
        self.register_buffer("bias", bias)
        self.kind = kind

    def forward(self, x, edge_index=None):
        raise NotImplementedError


class CompactModel(nn.Module):
    """Wraps a dense parent's state into the compact runtime form.

    `kind`: 'csr' (S1/S3) or 's4' (S4 dense fallback)."""

    def __init__(self, architecture: str, state: dict, kind: str):
        super().__init__()
        from .models import build_model
        self.arch = architecture
        self.kind = kind
        parent = build_model(architecture)
        parent.load_state_dict(state)
        self._build(parent)

    def _build(self, parent: nn.Module) -> None:
        from torch_geometric.nn import GCNConv

        cls = parent.__class__.__name__

        def lin(w_dense, bias):
            # stored [out, in]; the CSR projection computes (W_csr @ x^T)^T.
            # B1b: pass the dense (zeroed) weight; the CSR tensor is built on
            # demand (CSR tensors are not deepcopy-able in this torch build).
            return CSRLinear(w_dense.detach().clone(), bias)

        if cls == "MLP":
            self.m = nn.Sequential(
                lin(parent.net[0].weight, parent.net[0].bias),
                nn.ReLU(),
                lin(parent.net[2].weight, parent.net[2].bias),
                nn.ReLU(),
                lin(parent.net[4].weight, parent.net[4].bias),
            )
        elif cls == "CNN":
            # conv weight (out, in, k, k) -> CSR (out, in*k*k)
            c1, c2 = parent.conv1, parent.conv2
            self.m = nn.Sequential(
                CSRConv2d(c1.weight.detach().clone().flatten(1),
                          c1.bias, 5, 2, out_spatial=(28, 28)),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.MaxPool2d(2),
                CSRConv2d(c2.weight.detach().clone().flatten(1),
                          c2.bias, 5, 0, out_spatial=(10, 10)),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.MaxPool2d(2),
            )
            self.flatten = nn.Flatten(1)
            self.m2 = nn.Sequential(
                lin(parent.fc1.weight, parent.fc1.bias),
                nn.ReLU(),
                lin(parent.fc2.weight, parent.fc2.bias),
            )
        elif cls == "GCN":
            # GCNConv.lin.weight is stored [out, in]; the CSR projection uses
            # (W_csr @ x^T)^T so pass the stored [out, in] matrix directly.
            c1, c2 = parent.conv1, parent.conv2
            self.m = nn.Sequential(
                CSRGCNConv(c1.lin.weight.detach().clone(),
                           c1.bias, c1.in_channels, c1.out_channels),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Dropout(0.5),
                CSRGCNConv(c2.lin.weight.detach().clone(),
                           c2.bias, c2.in_channels, c2.out_channels),
            )
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"CompactModel: unsupported {cls}")

    def forward(self, x, edge_index=None):
        if self.arch == "gcn":
            return self._gcn(x, edge_index)
        if self.arch == "mlp":
            return self.m(x.flatten(1))
        x = self.m(x)
        return self.m2(self.flatten(x))

    def _gcn(self, x: torch.Tensor, edge_index: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # PyG message passing caches the normalized edge index on the module
        # (base GCNConv) during train-mode forwards; evaluation must use a
        # clean cache, exactly as the dense path's _fresh/clear protocol does.
        clear_gcn_caches(self)
        x = self.m[0](x, edge_index)
        x = self.m[1](x)
        x = self.m[2](x)
        x = self.m[3](x, edge_index)
        return x

"""CLI for the Lab 3 dense-reference package.

Usage: uv run python -m lab3 <cmd> --model {mlp,cnn,gcn} ...
Commands: make-splits, train, eval, bench.
Configs live in configs/<model>.yaml and hold the frozen hyperparameters.
CLI flags may override config values for tests only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import yaml
import torch

from .util import (
    CONFIGS_DIR,
    DATA_DIR,
    SPLIT_SEED,
    SPLITS_DIR,
    compute_splits_hash,
    set_threads,
)


def load_config(architecture: str) -> dict:
    path = CONFIGS_DIR / f"{architecture}.yaml"
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"missing config {path}")
    with open(path) as f:
        return yaml.safe_load(f)


def _cora_masks() -> tuple:
    from torch_geometric.datasets import Planetoid
    from .util import DATA_DIR as _D
    ds = Planetoid(root=str(_D / "Planetoid"), name="Cora")
    g = ds[0]
    return g.train_mask, g.val_mask, g.test_mask


def make_splits_impl() -> None:
    set_threads()
    import lab3.util as U
    existing = [p for p in U.SPLIT_FILES["fmnist"] + U.SPLIT_FILES["cora"] + [U.SPLITS_SHA]]
    if any(p.exists() for p in existing):
        raise FileExistsError("splits already exist; refusing to regenerate. "
                              "Delete splits/ manually only if you intend to reset all arms.")
    U.SPLITS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    np.random.seed(SPLIT_SEED)

    from .data import _fmnist_dataset
    train_ds = _fmnist_dataset("train")
    labels = np.asarray(train_ds.targets)
    assert labels.shape[0] == 60000
    val_idx = []
    for cls in range(10):
        pool = np.flatnonzero(labels == cls)
        val_idx.append(np.random.permutation(pool)[:500])
    val_idx = np.sort(np.concatenate(val_idx))
    train_idx = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(60000), val_idx, assume_unique=True)
    test_idx = np.arange(10000)
    assert train_idx.shape[0] == 55000 and val_idx.shape[0] == 5000

    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_train_idx.npy", train_idx.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_val_idx.npy", val_idx.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_test_idx.npy", test_idx.astype(np.int64))

    tr_m, va_m, te_m = _cora_masks()
    cora_tr = np.flatnonzero(tr_m.numpy())
    cora_va = np.flatnonzero(va_m.numpy())
    cora_te = np.flatnonzero(te_m.numpy())
    assert cora_tr.shape[0] == 140 and cora_va.shape[0] == 500 and cora_te.shape[0] == 1000
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "cora_train_idx.npy", cora_tr.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "cora_val_idx.npy", cora_va.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "cora_test_idx.npy", cora_te.astype(np.int64))

    U.SPLITS_SHA.write_text(compute_splits_hash() + "  splits/*.npy (fixed order, see compute_splits_hash)\n")
    print(f"splits written to {U.SPLITS_DIR}; hash={compute_splits_hash()}")


def _apply_overrides(cfg: dict, args) -> dict:
    """CLI flags override frozen config values (for tests only)."""
    for flag, key in (("--lr", "lr"), ("--weight-decay", "weight_decay"),
                      ("--batch-size", "batch_size"), ("--epochs", "max_epochs"),
                      ("--patience", "patience")):
        val = getattr(args, flag.replace("-", "_"), None)
        if val is not None:
            cfg[key] = val
    return cfg


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="lab3")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    p = sub.add_parser("make-splits")
    p.set_defaults(fn=make_splits_impl)

    def _make_calib():
        from .util import make_calib_split
        make_calib_split()

    p = sub.add_parser("make-calib", help="create the B.1 calibration subset once")
    p.set_defaults(fn=_make_calib)

    for name, help_ in (("train", "train a dense model"),
                        ("eval", "evaluate a saved checkpoint"),
                        ("bench", "benchmark a saved checkpoint"),
                        ("prune", "run one Part B sparsity arm")):
        p = sub.add_parser(name, help=help_)
        p.add_argument("--model", required=True, choices=["mlp", "cnn", "gcn"])
        p.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
        p.add_argument("--run-id", default=None)
        if name == "prune":
            p.add_argument("--no-bench", action="store_true",
                           help="skip the B.4 runtime paths (faster smoke)")
        # overrides (tests only)
        p.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=None)
        p.add_argument("--weight-decay", type=float, default=None)
        p.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=None)
        p.add_argument("--epochs", type=int, default=None)
        p.add_argument("--patience", type=int, default=None)

    # prune-specific flags
    p = sub.choices["prune"]
    # B1b: `dense_ft` is the B.6 control arm (fine-tune the dense parent with
    # the B.1 budget, no pruning); it uses target 0.0. The s1-s4 methods keep
    # their frozen targets.
    p.add_argument("--method", required=True,
                   choices=["s1", "s2", "s3", "s4", "dense_ft"])
    p.add_argument("--target", type=float, required=True,
                   choices=[0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9])

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    set_threads()

    if args.cmd == "make-splits":
        args.fn()
        return 0
    if args.cmd == "make-calib":
        args.fn()
        return 0

    cfg = load_config(args.model)
    cfg = _apply_overrides(cfg, args)

    if args.cmd == "train":
        from .training import train
        rec = train(args.model, cfg, seed=args.seed, run_id=args.run_id)
        print(f"run_id={rec['run_id']} best_epoch={rec['best_epoch']} "
              f"val_acc={rec['val_acc']:.4f} test_acc={rec['test_acc']:.4f} "
              f"epochs={rec['train_epochs']} wall={rec['wall_time_s']}s")
    elif args.cmd == "eval":
        from .evaln import eval as do_eval
        rec = do_eval(args.model, seed=args.seed)
        print(f"run_id={rec['run_id']} val_acc={rec['val_acc']:.4f} test_acc={rec['test_acc']:.4f}")
    elif args.cmd == "bench":
        from .bench import bench
        rec = bench(args.model, seed=args.seed)
        lat = rec["latency"]
        print(f"run_id={rec['run_id']} latency={lat} peak_rss={rec['peak_rss_bytes']}B")
    elif args.cmd == "prune":
        from .prune import prune
        out = prune(args.model, args.method, args.target, seed=args.seed,
                    bench=not getattr(args, "no_bench", False))
        for r in out["rows"]:
            if r.get("stage") in ("post_prune", "post_finetune"):
                p = r.get("paths", {})
                print(f"run_id={r['run_id']} arm_id={r['arm_id']} stage={r['stage']} "
                      f"val_acc={r['val_acc']:.4f} test_acc={r['test_acc']:.4f} "
                      f"achieved_sparsity={r['achieved_sparsity']:.4f} "
                      f"status={r['status']}")
                for pname, pdata in (p or {}).items():
                    if not isinstance(pdata, dict):
                        continue
                    lat = {k: v for k, v in pdata.items()
                           if isinstance(v, dict) and "median_ms" in v}
                    note = pdata.get("note", "")
                    print(f"  path={pname} runtime_status={pdata.get('runtime_status')} "
                          f"latency={lat} peak_rss={pdata.get('peak_rss_bytes')} "
                          f"bytes={pdata.get('dense_bytes') or pdata.get('compressed_bytes')}")
                    if note:
                        print(f"    note: {note}")
        print(f"arm_id={out['arm_id']} status={out['status']} reason={out['reason']} "
              f"wall={out['wall_time_s']}s")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Shared utilities: frozen environment setup, splits, run logging, code hash."""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch

# Repo root (project root): <root>/code/lab3/util.py -> parents[2]
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
DATA_DIR = ROOT / "data"
SPLITS_DIR = ROOT / "splits"
CHECKPOINTS_DIR = ROOT / "checkpoints" / "dense"
# P2: the results path is configurable via LAB3_RESULTS_DIR (tests point it at a
# tmp dir so pytest NEVER appends to the real results/runs.jsonl).
RESULTS_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("LAB3_RESULTS_DIR", str(ROOT / "results")))
CURVES_DIR = RESULTS_DIR / "curves"
RUNS_JSONL = RESULTS_DIR / "runs.jsonl"
BENCH_DIR = RESULTS_DIR / "bench"
FIGURES_DIR = ROOT / "figures"
CONFIGS_DIR = ROOT / "configs"

SPLIT_SEED = 12345
# B.1 (Part B): calibration subset — 1,024 TRAINING-split images, stratified
# 102-103 per class, drawn once with seed 12345. Labels are training labels.
CALIB_FILE = SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_calib_idx.npy"
CALIB_N = 1024
SPLIT_FILES = {
    "fmnist": [
        SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_train_idx.npy",
        SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_val_idx.npy",
        SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_test_idx.npy",
    ],
    "cora": [
        SPLITS_DIR / "cora_train_idx.npy",
        SPLITS_DIR / "cora_val_idx.npy",
        SPLITS_DIR / "cora_test_idx.npy",
    ],
}
SPLITS_SHA = SPLITS_DIR / "SPLITS.sha256"


def set_threads() -> None:
    """Frozen thread protocol: 4 intra-op threads, 1 inter-op thread."""
    torch.set_num_threads(4)
    try:
        torch.set_num_interop_threads(1)
    except RuntimeError:
        # interop thread count can only be set before any parallel region starts
        pass


def set_seed(seed: int) -> None:
    """Frozen seed protocol: Python random, NumPy, and PyTorch."""
    random.seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)


def _sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def compute_splits_hash() -> str:
    """SHA-256 over the six split index files (fixed order, name + array bytes)."""
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    for key in ("fmnist", "cora"):
        for path in SPLIT_FILES[key]:
            h.update(path.name.encode("utf-8"))
            h.update(_sha256_file(path).encode("ascii"))
    return h.hexdigest()


def make_calib_split() -> None:
    """B.1: create splits/fmnist_calib_idx.npy exactly once and APPEND its
    hash line to SPLITS.sha256 (never regenerate the other splits)."""
    if CALIB_FILE.exists():
        raise FileExistsError(
            f"{CALIB_FILE} already exists; the calibration subset is created once "
            "and never regenerated. Delete it manually only if you intend to reset.")
    np.random.seed(SPLIT_SEED)
    from .data import _fmnist_dataset
    train_ds = _fmnist_dataset("train")
    labels = np.asarray(train_ds.targets)
    train_idx = load_indices("fmnist")["train"]
    train_set = set(int(i) for i in train_idx)
    # 1024 = 10 * 102 + 4: the first 4 classes get 103, the rest 102.
    per = [103 if c < 4 else 102 for c in range(10)]
    assert sum(per) == CALIB_N
    calib = []
    for c in range(10):
        pool = np.asarray(sorted(i for i in train_idx if labels[int(i)] == c))
        assert set(labels[int(i)] for i in pool).issubset({c})
        calib.append(np.random.permutation(pool)[: per[c]])
    calib_idx = np.sort(np.concatenate(calib)).astype(np.int64)
    assert calib_idx.shape[0] == CALIB_N
    assert set(int(i) for i in calib_idx).issubset(train_set), "calib must be subset of train"
    np.save(CALIB_FILE, calib_idx)
    line = f"{_sha256_file(CALIB_FILE)}  {CALIB_FILE.name}\n"
    with open(SPLITS_SHA, "a") as f:
        f.write(line)
    print(f"calibration subset written to {CALIB_FILE}; appended hash to {SPLITS_SHA}")


def verify_splits() -> None:
    """Load all split files and verify SPLITS.sha256; never regenerates."""
    if not SPLITS_SHA.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"{SPLITS_SHA} not found. Run `uv run python -m lab3 make-splits` first. "
            "Splits are never regenerated automatically."
        )
    for key in SPLIT_FILES:
        for path in SPLIT_FILES[key]:
            if not path.exists():
                raise FileNotFoundError(f"missing split file {path}; run make-splits first")
    recorded = SPLITS_SHA.read_text().strip().split()[0]
    actual = compute_splits_hash()
    if actual != recorded:
        raise ValueError(
            f"split hash mismatch: recorded {recorded} != actual {actual}. "
            "Refusing to continue; run make-splits only if you intentionally reset splits."
        )


def load_indices(name: str) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    verify_splits()
    out = {}
    files = {"train": SPLIT_FILES[name][0], "val": SPLIT_FILES[name][1], "test": SPLIT_FILES[name][2]}
    for k, p in files.items():
        out[k] = np.load(p)
    return out


def code_hash() -> str:
    """SHA-256 over all files under code/ (git-free: pure file-content hash)."""
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    code_dir = ROOT / "code"
    for path in sorted(code_dir.rglob("*")):
        if path.is_file():
            h.update(str(path.relative_to(code_dir)).encode("utf-8"))
            h.update(path.read_bytes())
    return h.hexdigest()


def _ensure_dirs() -> None:
    # P2: tests redirect LAB3_RESULTS_DIR at a tmp dir; only the results tree is
    # created there. DATA_DIR / SPLITS_DIR / FIGURES_DIR already exist in the repo
    # (never created under a redirected results root).
    for d in (RESULTS_DIR, CURVES_DIR, BENCH_DIR):
        d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


def new_run_id(architecture: str, method: str = "dense") -> str:
    ts = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%fZ")
    return f"{architecture}-{method}-{ts}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}"


def write_run_record(rec: dict) -> None:
    """Append one JSON line to results/runs.jsonl. Never rewrites or deletes."""
    _ensure_dirs()
    with open(RUNS_JSONL, "a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(rec, default=str) + "\n")
        f.flush()
        os.fsync(f.fileno())


def prior_bench_run_ids(architecture: str, seed: int = 0) -> list[str]:
    """run_ids of all earlier successful `bench` records for this (arch, seed), in
    file order. Used to fill `supersedes` on a corrected re-bench. The log is
    append-only: earlier lines are never edited or deleted."""
    out = []
    if not RUNS_JSONL.exists():
        return out
    with open(RUNS_JSONL) as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            try:
                r = json.loads(line)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                continue
            if (r.get("command") == "bench" and r.get("status") == "ok"
                    and r.get("architecture") == architecture and r.get("seed") == seed):
                out.append(r["run_id"])
    return out


def versions() -> dict:
    import platform

    return {
        "python": platform.python_version(),
        "torch": torch.__version__,
        "numpy": np.__version__,
        "platform": platform.platform(),
    }


def base_record(architecture: str, command: str) -> dict:
    return {
        "run_id": new_run_id(architecture),
        "status": "ok",
        "reason": None,
        "part": "A",
        "architecture": architecture,
        "method": "dense",
        "target_sparsity": 0.0,
        "achieved_sparsity": 0.0,
        "stored_precision": "fp32",
        "compute_precision": "fp32",
        "accumulator_precision": "fp32",
        "seed": None,
        "train_epochs": None,
        "finetune_epochs": 0,
        "best_epoch": None,
        "val_acc": None,
        "val_loss": None,
        "test_acc": None,
        "total_params": None,
        "nonzero_params": None,
        "dense_bytes": None,
        "raw_tensor_bytes": None,
        # P1: compressed_bytes is reserved for the compact-export artifact
        # (Part B path 2). gzip_bytes is the gzip-9 size of the dense state_dict
        # file and is reported for every run (dense included).
        "compressed_bytes": None,
        "gzip_bytes": None,
        "est_macs": None,
        "est_macs_nonzero": None,
        "est_macs_sparse_input": None,
        "gcn_norm_macs": None,
        "peak_rss_bytes": None,
        "rss_before_model_bytes": None,
        "model_rss_delta_bytes": None,
        "latency": {},
        "parent_run_id": None,
        "supersedes": [],
        "wall_time_s": None,
        "code_hash": code_hash(),
        "versions": versions(),
        "timestamp": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "command": command,
    }


def finalize_record(rec: dict, *, status: str | None = None, reason: str | None = None) -> dict:
    if status is not None:
        rec["status"] = status
        rec["reason"] = reason
    return rec


def run_wall_timer(rec: dict, t0: float) -> dict:
    rec["wall_time_s"] = round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 3)
    return rec
